subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should native compaction be allowed to persist exactly one explicitly marked partial result after the wrapper-owned safety timeout aborts, but only while the same timeout reason's bounded settlement token remains open?
rationale: The implementation is technically bounded and well tested, but accepting session mutation after an externally observed timeout is a product-level session-state and hook-ordering policy that source inspection cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept bounded partial commit
options.body: Allow the marked partial result to commit within the reason-owned window, preventing deterministic restarts while preserving fail-closed behavior for every other abort path.

options.title: Remain strictly fail-closed
options.body: Reject every result after timeout and pursue a different architecture such as durable per-chunk checkpoints committed before the timeout boundary.

options.title: Narrow the accepted lifecycle
options.body: Permit the partial commit but require post-commit hook completion or another explicit sequencing contract before the wrapper reports success.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded partial commit
recommendation.body: Allow the marked partial result to commit within the reason-owned window, preventing deterministic restarts while preserving fail-closed behavior for every other abort path.
